title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 22, 2026: KOSPI -3.52%, KOSDAQ -3.62% as AI Cost Worries Return
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,533.77, down 3.52%, and KOSDAQ closed at 764.10, down 3.62%, as profit-taking and renewed worries about AI data center costs erased the previous day's rebound. Individual themes moved on their own news: AI agents and physical AI, Vinatech's expanded supercapacitor contracts, an unconfirmed rumor about Kim Jong Un, and U.S. President Trump's comments on a Ukraine ceasefire.

1. Profit-taking and AI investment worries — KOSPI and KOSDAQ fall together

KOSPI fell 201.89 points (-3.52%) to 5,533.77 and KOSDAQ fell 28.66 points (-3.62%) to 764.10. After the sharp rebound the day before, sellers took profits, and renewed concern about the cost and profitability of AI data center investment widened selling, led by large semiconductor stocks. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix both weakened and weighed on the indexes.

2. AI agents and physical AI — AI-related stocks in focus

Expectations continued that AI will move beyond generative AI toward agents that perform real work and physical AI that operates on industrial sites. The government's plan to expand physical AI funding and build a public-private ecosystem drew attention to companies with related technology. SKAI was highlighted for its past participation in a government-led physical AI alliance, and news of AI cooperation in manufacturing supported the theme. Names in focus included SKAI, AgentAI, Polaris AI, Saltlux, Konan Technology, Selvas AI, Flitto and Elice. No single new disclosure applied to all of them, and some moves reflect theme-driven buying on industry growth expectations.

3. Vinatech's data center supercapacitor contracts grow — Bloom Energy supply chain in focus

Vinatech rose on reports that it has secured a string of supercapacitor supply contracts for data centers. According to reports, contracts including those with Indian and Taiwanese companies total about 242.4 billion won. A separate 123 billion won contract to supply Bloom Energy through U.S. power equipment maker ACBEL POLYTECH had been disclosed earlier. Expectations rose that AI data center expansion will increase demand for parts that keep power stable and handle sudden power swings, and attention also turned to Bloom Energy's upcoming earnings. Vinatech, Coses and Hansun Engineering were in focus. Vinatech has confirmed supply contracts, but the direct supply relationship with Bloom Energy and the business links of the other stocks differ and should be checked separately.

4. Unconfirmed Kim Jong Un rumor spreads on overseas social media — defense stocks in focus

Defense and North Korea tension stocks drew attention as a rumor about the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un spread on overseas social media. Victek, Speco, Hanil Forging and Huneed Technologies were in focus. The claim is unconfirmed and no evidence was presented. North Korean state media reported that Kim attended a public event, and South Korean diplomatic and security authorities said they had no information supporting the claim. The move should be read as a short-term theme reaction to a rumor, and volatility in these stocks calls for caution.

5. Trump says a Ukraine ceasefire is close — reconstruction stocks in focus

U.S. President Donald Trump said a deal to end the war between Russia and Ukraine is closer than it has been in some time, raising hopes for postwar rebuilding. He said talks are at a sensitive stage and that he would not rush additional sanctions, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also mentioned freezing fighting at current lines while pursuing diplomacy. No final agreement has been reached. Daemo, Jeonjin Construction Robot and Hyundai Everdigm drew attention on expectations that road and construction infrastructure repair would raise demand for heavy equipment.

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI fall on Oct 22?
Profit-taking after the previous day's rebound and renewed concern about AI data center costs led to selling in large chip stocks. KOSPI closed at 5,533.77 (-3.52%) and KOSDAQ at 764.10 (-3.62%).

Is the Kim Jong Un rumor true?
It is unconfirmed and no evidence was presented. North Korean state media reported his attendance at a public event, and South Korean authorities said they had no supporting information.

Has a Ukraine ceasefire been agreed?
No. Trump said a deal was close, but no final agreement has been reached.
